title: 2006 HMMT February Algebra Problem 2
statement: Find all real solutions \((x, y)\) of the system \(x^{2}+y=12=y^{2}+x\).

solutions.text: We have \(x^{2}+y=y^{2}+x\) which can be written as \((x-y)(x+y-1)=0\). The case \(x=y\) yields \(x^{2}+x-12=0\), hence \((x, y)=(3,3)\) or \((-4,-4)\). The case \(y=1-x\) yields \(x^{2}+1-x-12=x^{2}-x-11=0\) which has solutions \(x=\frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1+44}}{2}=\frac{1 \pm 3 \sqrt{5}}{2}\). The other two solutions follow.
